plain: The shared pipeline where you and AWS both write down the deals you're working.
real: If it isn't in ACE, AWS doesn't know it exists and nobody gets credit for it.

plain: Did the partner bring the deal, or help win one AWS already had?
real: Who gets the credit. This is why the meeting ran long.

plain: A negotiated price, transacted through AWS Marketplace instead of a normal contract.
real: The customer pays with money they already promised AWS. That's usually the whole reason it's on the table.

plain: A badge confirming AWS checked that you're genuinely good at one specific thing.
real: Months of paperwork and customer references. Also the thing that gets you into certain rooms.

plain: Your seller and an AWS seller work the same deal together.
real: Two comp plans pointed at one customer. Works beautifully, or not even slightly.

plain: Market Development Funds — money from AWS to pay for marketing you do together.
real: It arrives with paperwork and a deadline, and it expires whether you spend it or not.

plain: The one sentence explaining why a customer should buy both things together.
real: Written by committee, which is why it's three sentences and commits to nothing. I have written several.

plain: We'll talk about it after this call.
real: Someone currently on this call should not hear the answer.
